newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down in active trading on Tuesday due to overnight heavy losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 19,540 yuan ($2,354) per tonne, losing 430 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 19,400 and hit a high of 19,550.
January fell 420 to 19,480, February 420 to 19,530, March 400 to 19,530, May 370 to 19,530 and June 220 to 19,640.
Combined volume rose sharply to 110,480 tonnes from 37,730.
Copper opened down but short-covering pushed prices off lows with most contracts closing at or near their intra-day highs.
Traders said LME losses triggered heavy selling but many short position holders liquidated their positions at low levels.
"Panic selling emerged in the morning session with many investors expecting copper to accelarate its downward movement in the next few days," one trader said.
"But drops in open interest indicated the downward momentum had decreased a lot," he added.
"Market sentiment was badly hurt after copper breached the key 20,000-yuan support level several days ago," a second trader said.
"Copper is not likely to rebound to above 20,000 yuan in the short term," he added.
Analysts expect copper to test the 19,000-yuan support level in the next few days.
